- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.6) and forecast is high, reduce forecast slightly to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.2) and forecast is low, increase forecast modestly to avoid underreaction.  
- If recent price spike is followed by forecast overshoot, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.  
- If forecast consistently lags true price by 1–2 days, adjust forward-looking models to include 1-day lead-in sentiment weight.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is >2σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–15%.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, smooth forecast transitions to avoid abrupt directional shifts.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.4) and price is volatile, reduce forecast variance by 20–30% to avoid overfitting noise.
